description: Tessera-wire container, served by Tessera's OWN vLLM plugin: package `tessera.serving`, entry point `tessera = "tessera.serving:register"` under [project.entry-points."vllm.general_plugins"], registering quant_method = "tessera". PrismaQuant never vendors the serving runtime; the boundary crosses through prismaquant/tessera_runtime/tessera_serving_runtime_pin.json and the contract the plugin packages (tessera/serving/runtime_contract.json). THERE IS NO ENABLE FLAG: the checkpoint's `quantization_config.quant_method: "tessera"` selects the plugin, and the single operator knob is TESSERA_SERVE_MODE=resident|streamed, which is declared rather than defaulted because it changes the footprint the artifact occupies and is folded into vLLM's compile-cache key. The serve installs the plugin into the vanilla vLLM image with `pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation -e <tessera>`; no vLLM patch, no forked runtime. The reference serve script is /home/rob/tessera/experiments/tessera_plugin_served.sh and the route census is /home/rob/tessera/tools/tessera_route_census.py -- both live in the Tessera repository, which this repository does not vendor, so they are NAMED here and not copied.
wired_architectures_note: qwen3 is the profile whose two fused groups Tessera's exporter stacks one-blob-per-vLLM-module, and whose 0.6B checkpoint was served from a PrismaQuant allocation on the plugin (2026-09-02). Moved here from tests/test_profile_export_lanes.py's TESSERA_WIRED on 2026-09-03: the roster is a decision and belongs beside the lane it decides. Declaring the lane does not satisfy its build gates: preflight requires the pinned packaged runtime contract for both the imported package and external producer checkout, plus assignment and priced-input coverage. The v2 pin does not require a release tag.

gates.description: Fresh vanilla vLLM container with the pinned Tessera plugin editable-installed, TP=1, speculative decode off, --enforce-eager, then greedy completions over the OpenAI endpoint. Repeat for TESSERA_SERVE_MODE=streamed: the two residencies decode the same bytes by different paths, so an eager receipt in one mode is not a receipt for the other.

A second fresh container under vLLM's default compiled forward and CUDA graphs. Eager success cannot stand in for compiled load/capture/generation success on this lane in particular: the compile-cache identity key has to carry the residency mode, and a mode-blind key is only visible under capture. GLM-5.3 (GLM5-next) is the exception, and its graph leg is the release serve configuration rather than the default: --compilation-config '{"mode":"NONE","cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' with VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 (RobTand/prismaquant#1864, tessera#774). vLLM never compiles that model, yet its default VLLM_COMPILE resolves custom_ops to none and the norm IR ops to native, so every custom op in the served prefill runs its eager fallback (tessera#702 cause 1); mode NONE resolves them as the eager leg does. Under mode NONE nothing is torch-compiled, so the GLM-5.3 graph leg exercises capture but not the compile-cache key. Its limits: decode under FULL graphs past max_model_len 2048 is not eager-equivalent on image 5be13705 (tessera#702 cause 2), and the MTP drafter under graphs has no receipt (tessera#695). This lane's reference script is single-box TP 1 and cannot serve the GLM-5.3 artifact; that serve runs at TP 2 outside this repository.

Principle 12's second leg on this lane: the per-module route histogram the serve actually emitted, read from the plugin's own telemetry, compared against the artifact's priced activation_contracts. A bpp or KL number whose units rode a route other than the one they were priced on is not a result. The tool lives in the Tessera repository and is named, not vendored. THIS GATE CARRIED `shipcard_slot: null` UNTIL 2026-09-03, which meant the one principle-12 check this lane declares was recorded nowhere and could be refused on by nothing -- the exact `named but never run` shape RobTand/prismaquant#119 describes. It is now a lane-scoped required slot (shipcard.LANE_SCOPED_SLOTS), opened by the arm and refused on by publish_artifact until a real census closes it. The census closes via `python -m prismaquant.shipcard_cli fill-route-census`, which verify replays from the carried records; a serve that ran on the substitute decoder refuses there (PrismaQuant #136).

gates.runner: TESSERA_ROUTE_TRACE=<routes-rank<N>.json> on every rank of an eager serve, then python -m prismaquant.shipcard_cli fill-route-trace <shipcard.json> --trace <routes-rank0.json> [--trace <routes-rank1.json> ...] --expected-ranks <world-size>
gates.description: Principle 14's serve-side leg (PrismaQuant #575). Every rank of a serve started with TESSERA_ROUTE_TRACE writes the plugin's own tessera.route_trace/1 counters. fill-route-trace compares, per rank and per token count, the module count served under each (route family, kind, activation contract) with the count the artifact's config.json prices under the contract the pinned runtime executes on the card's platform, and refuses on any difference, naming the contracts and counts. The trace names no modules, so the comparison is a histogram, not a per-module map. A missing, unreadable, empty or compiled (M*) rank trace is NOT VERIFIED: the slot stays unfilled and publish_artifact refuses the card. verify replays the comparison from the carried traces against the current packaged contract, so a hand-set passed flag closes nothing.
Unchanged from the native lane: same validator, same endpoint kind, same thresholds. The ship gate is runtime-agnostic and always was.

Run inside the plugin serving container through vLLM's offline LLM API. Exact full-vocab KL-vs-BF16 scores each stored teacher window's final position; --score-positions all uses prompt top-K and is a different metric. Generate the image-matched BF16 teacher payload with the same tool's --mode teacher first. Match extension residency across A/B arms: the NVFP4 route builds one CUDA extension on first use, and loading a CUDA extension shifts allocator addresses.
Run inside the plugin serving container through vLLM's offline LLM API. Direct WikiText PPL on the Tessera artifact uses the exact CPU-materialized, value-closed offline token payload.

gates.runner: python ${TESSERA_REPO}/experiments/uniform_control.py verify <artifact> <matched-byte-uniform-artifact> --params <quantizable-parameters> --candidate-kl <same-protocol-candidate-kl> --control-kl <same-protocol-control-kl> --metric <declared-metric> --max-relative-slack <predeclared-byte-slack> --report <control-block.json> && python -m prismaquant.shipcard_cli fill-control <shipcard.json> --control-block <control-block.json> --control-record <served-control-kl.json> --control-model-dir <matched-byte-uniform-artifact> --gold-metric-key kl_mean
gates.description: Expose the existing Tessera accountant and shipcard fill path for the conditional matched-byte control requirement. Choose the control family, integer-bit matching rule and byte slack before measurement; add --require-no-larger if that is the predeclared rule. Quantizable parameters exclude allocator-pinned regions. A4/A8 labels or pairwise KL alone do not establish byte matching. The control must be exported and served under the candidate's exact teacher/calibration/runtime protocol. Preserve the producer block and control's own served KL; the unchanged verifier replays both. An unserved block, missing control evidence or a failed comparison remains a refusal. This declaration launches nothing and supplies no override.

producer_tools.description: The ONLY place the Tessera wire is written, as the supported package entry point `python -m tessera.export_serving` (RobTand/tessera#687, schema tessera.serving_plan.v1). PrismaQuant writes the plan itself (prismaquant/tessera_plan_writer.py, #1587: the spelling and the charged-bits accounting are the producer's records, not the exporter's); the arm hands the exporter the plan and the priced inputs unchanged. Requires a Tessera pin at #687 or later: at the 38e96012 pin this file is absent and the preflight refuses, which is the fail-closed state until the pin moves.

campaign_tools.description: Public installed producer CLI publishing expert_projection.v1. Explicit python= takes precedence over TESSERA_PRODUCER_PYTHON, then the caller interpreter is the standalone default. All campaign/MTP preflights and requests use that one selection; a newer producer package need not replace the pinned serving package. Checkpoint headers, source seals, expert geometry and digest-cache behavior remain exporter-owned. No sibling checkout, experiments import, runtime/export pin change or serving qualification follows.

kl_evaluator.note: The producer-side frontier evaluator, reachable because tessera_render renders a Tessera rung through the tessera package: a frontier KL measures the same decode the serve executes. Selection on this lane is SURROGATE by default; nothing here is promoted.

served_activation_quantization.rationale: DERIVED, not hand-asserted (principle 14). Every glob is a formats[] row's `name_pattern` with `{k}` replaced by `*`, read out of the packaged tessera/serving/runtime_contract.json, and each family's A-side contract is the `activation_contract` that same row publishes. TESSERA_E2M1_K2 executes `e2m1_group16_ue4m3_static` -- W4A4: the decoded tile IS the stock NVFP4 tile and the route runs torch._scaled_mm on quantized activations. TESSERA_E4M3_K1 executes `fp8_per_token_dynamic` -- W8A8: the decoded tile is the stock per-channel FP8 pair with per-token dynamic activation scales. TESSERA_BF16_K1 executes `bf16_unquantized` -- W16A16: the decoded tile is a plain bf16 tensor and the route runs the stock BF16 GEMM, so this is the ONE family whose A side genuinely costs nothing, and it says so with a value rather than by omission. That distinction is the reason the field moved onto the formats[] row in Tessera's contract v4: published only on lane_eligibility cells, a family with no receipt yet -- which BF16 is, `attested_rungs_q256` is empty -- had its activation contract in changelog prose, and a consumer could not tell 'unquantised by design' from 'nobody filled it in'. Being listed here is not permission to ship: the eligibility gate reads the CELLS, not this list. As of Tessera contract v5 all three families have cells -- BF16 gained two (sm_121 dense, decode and batch) on the q256=1792 receipt -- so what the gate now refuses is a RUNG outside `attested_rungs_q256`, which is [896] / [1024] / [1792], one point each. Every other rung in every family's reader range still resolves unattested, and that is the rule holding rather than bending.
served_activation_quantization.executes_by_platform_rationale: DERIVED from lane_eligibility.platforms[*].executes in the packaged tessera/serving/runtime_contract.json, and refused on drift by tessera_export_lane.require_platform_executes_derived_from_contract -- the same rule the flat `executes` list above is held to, asked per platform. The two are not redundant: `executes` says what a family's route RUNS, which is true wherever that family is served, while this says whether it is served THERE, which nothing about the family implies. Contract v23 (lane schema v10) is the first that can state it: before v10 a platforms entry was a bare KEY, so the only way to say anything about a device was to have served on it, and a cell is a receipt -- there was no way to publish `this family has no native route on this device`, and silence had to stand in for it. null now says it, and it is a claim somebody looked. What ships today: sm_121 backs all three families; gfx1151 (Strix Halo, RDNA3.5) and gfx1201 (RDNA4) back TESSERA_BF16_K1 only, which is the Tessera-16 W16A16 lane, and publish null for the two quantized families because the pinned runtime has no native route for those bytes on those devices -- not because a kernel is unwritten. THIS MAP IS STILL ONLY A PRICE: the eligibility gate reads the CELLS. At contract v24 the two platforms diverge there, and this map does not move with them -- gfx1201 gained two TESSERA_BF16_K1 dense cells at rung 1792 (decode and batch), so route_status_for answers backed_with_serve_flag for that family and rung on that device, while gfx1151 has no cell and still answers `unattested` with source :no_cell for every family. Both still answer :no_cell for TESSERA_E4M3_K1 and TESSERA_E2M1_K2, and so does gfx1201 for any BF16 rung other than 1792 (:rung_not_listed) through contract v29. At contract v31 (Tessera #551, PrismaQuant #699) the eight dense cells withdraw and gfx1201 carries no cell at all, so every family answers `unattested` with source :no_cell on both AMD platforms; the executes map above does not move with that withdrawal. A non-null value here is not permission to ship; it is permission to price.
served_activation_quantization.why_this_matters: The A-side term is what stops the allocator comparing a W4A4 Tessera rung against a W8A8 or a W16A16 one as if the activation side were free. Pricing an A side the runtime does not execute -- or failing to price one it does -- is a CURRENCY error, and it moved a whole 87 GB DSv4 allocation once (2026-08-17, NVFP4_CB). Two of the three families genuinely quantize activations and are priced for it; the third does not, and is priced at 16 bits rather than at zero by default.
served_activation_quantization.if_this_changes: The preflight asserts EQUALITY against the packaged table: tests/test_tessera_lane_admission.py::test_lane_spec_executes_is_derived_from_the_packaged_contract rebuilds this list from tessera/serving/runtime_contract.json and refuses any drift, and the same test pins each family's activation contract. So this field is not maintained by hand -- a runtime that adds a family, retires one, or changes a family's executed contract makes that test fail, and the fix is to re-read the table, never to edit this list to silence it.

notes: ADMISSION IS PINNED TO AN EXACT TESSERA COMMIT AND CONTRACT DIGEST, NOT TO A RELEASE TAG (changed 2026-09-04 on Rob's instruction: 'we won't have to keep cutting releases'). prismaquant/tessera_runtime/tessera_serving_runtime_pin.json carries commit, version and contract_sha256; require_pinned_tessera_runtime refuses unless the pin equals the reader's constants AND the INSTALLED tessera/serving/runtime_contract.json hashes to the pinned digest -- so a Tessera checkout on PYTHONPATH that is not the pinned one still answers False for every rung, exactly as the PENDING sentinels did. version_is_release is recorded and advisory; no gate reads it. Moving the pin is one reviewed commit editing the JSON and the module constants together; nothing else in this repository flips the answer.

DENSE-ONLY -- BY EVIDENCE SINCE CONTRACT v17. The packaged contract DECLARES routed_moe and carries four routed_moe cells (through contract v29 it carried four; at v17 it carried two, both publishing the measurement that refuses them: evidence.smoke.status "repetitive", the runtime's own record that a greedy smoke on that route degenerated). At contract v31 the TESSERA_E4M3_K1 pair publishes smoke.status "recorded" and the TESSERA_E2M1_K2 pair "not_recorded". PrismaQuant refuses by reading that field (lane_eligibility.cell_evidence_admits), not by a structure ban it typed: principle 9 requires a route to generate correctly, and cell_evidence_admits is status-only, so "recorded" and "not_recorded" pass and admitting those rows rides the pin review (PrismaQuant #198). Until v17 the contract declared only dense and absence was the honest state; now the claim exists and the evidence is what admits or refuses it. Promoting routed MoE is a decision on the evidence and it is Rob's.

TP UP TO 2 SINCE CONTRACT v29 (Tessera #517, PrismaQuant #632). Every tensor_parallel unit declares max_world_size 2 and cites the served TP2 receipt glm53_a4_stub_tp2_sm121, which the reader requires to be published, to have executed the unit and to have served at least that world; tessera_tp_world_attested refuses any larger degree. Through contract v24 every unit declared 1. expert_parallel.units is empty.
Both residency modes (TESSERA_SERVE_MODE=resident|streamed) are receipted by the contract's cells and must both be exercised: they decode the same bytes by different paths.
Gates are ADVISORY on this lane as on every other (R16's open half is deferred to Robert); the shipcard is what refuses.

THE ARM EXISTS AND VENDORS NOTHING. `EXPORT_CONTAINER=tessera` in run-pipeline.sh writes the serving plan with PrismaQuant's own prismaquant/tessera_plan_writer.py (#1587: the TESSERA_<BASE>_K<arity>_R<rung> spelling and the charged-bits accounting are the producer's records, so the translation lives on this side of the boundary) and encodes it by calling Tessera's supported exporter `python -m tessera.export_serving` under $TESSERA_REPO (RobTand/tessera#687), the same named-not-vendored boundary this spec already uses for tessera_plugin_served.sh and tools/tessera_route_census.py. export_native_compressed.py still has no Tessera codec and must not grow one: a wire recipe with two homes is how the two halves of one format drift apart. The arm's preflight is prismaquant/tessera_export_lane.py (declared structure, principle-14 executes derivation, release pin, supported producer tool present) and it refuses today on the pin alone -- so this spec's bar is now something a run reaches rather than something only a future exporter is built against.
